## Bildmuseet, Umeå

Set beside the Ume River on Umeå Arts Campus, Bildmuseet is one of Sweden’s leading venues for international contemporary art. Part of Umeå University, the museum occupies a striking seven-storey building with a wooden façade, offering exhibitions spanning art, photography, design and architecture. Beyond the exhibitions, Bildmuseet hosts talks, workshops and occasional Art Friday events, ranging from exhibition openings and film screenings to quizzes and live music.

Since opening in Stockholm in 2010, Fotografiska has expanded to cities including Berlin, Tallinn, Shanghai and Shenzhen. Located on Södermalm, this photography museum has no permanent collection, instead presenting changing exhibitions by established and emerging photographers from around the world. Open until late in the evening, it also hosts talks and events. Round off your visit at the award-winning restaurant, serving seasonal food with panoramic views across the water.

Housed in a former boiler house beneath the Älvsborg Bridge in Gothenburg, Röda Sten Konsthall has a colourful past. Once a venue for rave parties and threatened with demolition, the industrial building is now a hub for contemporary art, showcasing sculpture, installations, photography and video art. The gallery also hosts talks and workshops and organises the Gothenburg International Biennial for Contemporary Art (GIBCA), held across the city. The next edition runs from 4 September to 21 November 2027.

With a focus on contemporary and public art, Borås Konstmuseum showcases Swedish and international artists through painting, sculpture, photography and moving images. Admission is free, and visitors can explore exhibitions, guided tours and creative activities. Since 2008, the museum has organised the Borås International Sculpture Biennial, with the next edition in 2028. Beyond the museum, use its digital art map to discover sculptures, murals and other public artworks around the city – and see why Borås is known as ‘the sculpture city’.

### The museum is temporarily closed due to renovation – but we will return even stronger in spring 2027.

For 14 months, Trapholt will be closed to visitors as the museum undergoes a major transformation. We’re expanding, renovating, and reimagining – with a focus on sustainability, improved accessibility, more opportunities, and even more space for communication and community. The vision is clear: Trapholt will be a cultural beacon and green haven that invites even more people to experience world-class art and design.

The renovation doesn’t mean we’re disappearing – quite the opposite. During this period, we’ll be present throughout Kolding with Trapholt To Go, workshops, school projects, and events. Trapholt comes to you while we build the museum of the future.

The renovation will begin on January 1, 2026. The last day the museum is open to the public will be December 30, 2025, and we expect to reopen on March 1, 2027. You can already look forward to a big reopening celebration!

The renovation of Trapholt began with an architectural competition, announced as an EU public tender with prior prequalification. This ensures that the project complies with EU regulations for public construction and guarantees an open, transparent, and fair competition.

Even though the building will be closed, the museum will still be active. We’ll continue to work on future exhibitions and everything else that typically happens behind the scenes. Additionally, through the projects _Trapholt To Go_ and _Trapholt Pop Up_, we’ll move out into Kolding Municipality with art projects, events, and educational programs. We’ll visit schools, take part in city events, and bring the Trapholt spirit into new spaces – we look forward to meeting you out there!

■ In spring 2027, a new hub for conservation, exhibition and creation will open in Massy, Essonne: Centre Pompidou Francilien – fabrique de l’art.

Following the gradual closure of all levels of the historic Beaubourg building, the major renovation project—entrusted to the architectural firms AIA Life Designers (technical component) and Moreau Kusunoki (cultural component), in collaboration with Frida Escobedo Studio—will begin in early 2026.

This undertaking combines technical and environmental components, such as the complete asbestos removal from the façade, treatment of corrosion on the main structure, renovation and energy optimization of the building, and improvements to accessibility. It also encompasses cultural aspects: enhancing the visitor experience, rethinking the display of the collection and the layout of the Bpi (Public Information Library), reconfiguring spatial organization to allow for greater emphasis on creation, and thereby reaffirming Centre Pompidou’s multidisciplinary identity.

Although the renovation work on Centre Pompidou will not officially begin until early 2026, its spaces will gradually close to the public throughout 2025 to allow the teams to relocate under the best possible conditions. The building will close its doors on 22 September 2025 and offers one final festive event within its walls on 24 and 25 October 2025, Because Beabourg.

The Public Information Library (Bpi) moves to the 12th arrondissement of Paris, into the Lumière building, which opens its doors on August 25, 2025, with the same hours and access conditions. As for Centre’s cinema and the Bpi's "Cinémathèque du documentaire" activities, they will be hosted at the mk2 bibliothèque, BNF-François Mitterand entrance, refurbished and renamed mk2 bibliothèque x Centre Pompidou for the occasion, starting in September 2025. Studio 13/16 will relocate in spring 2026 to a nearby location—the Gaîté Lyrique in the 3rd arrondissement. Only Ircam will remain in its historic location on Place Stravinsky, at the heart of a cultural activation program led by Centre Pompidou, ensuring that the Plateau Beaubourg (Beaubourg neighborhood) continues to be a vibrant cultural hub.

■ In autumn 2025, its iconic Parisian building will close for renovation works aimed at reconnecting, by 2030, with its original utopian vision.

Historically known for its generous practice of lending works abroad, Centre Pompidou has, over the past decade, developed an original and ambitious model of international development, extending its reach from Málaga to Shanghai, via Brussels, Seoul and Foz do Iguaçu in Brazil through medium-term collaborations. The unprecedented context of the closure of its Paris building for renovation offers it a unique opportunity to establish new tailor-made international partnerships and to circulate a series of exhibitions drawn from the excellence of the collection of the Musée National d’Art Moderne.

Designed by the architectural firm PCA-Stream, this innovative, restrained and resilient building is intended to become a true living space for the residents of the Île-de-France region, just 30 minutes from Paris thanks to the forthcoming Line 18 of the Grand Paris Express. Just as Centre Pompidou in Beaubourg opens onto the city through its Piazza and iconic escalator, Centre Pompidou Francilien engages in dialogue with its immediate environment: nature. Extending towards the Parc de la Blanchette and its lake, its façade features large wooden walkways, a planted stairway, and a panoramic terrace.
